title: Document Claude Code native tools available to agents
description:
Reference list of Claude Code harness-native tools (not MCP, not LETS plugin) for awareness when building commands and agents. Useful when deciding whether a feature can be done with built-ins or needs MCP/external integration.

## Always-loaded (8) - used every session

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Bash | Execute shell commands |
| Read | Read file from filesystem |
| Edit | Exact string replacement in files |
| Write | Create/overwrite file |
| Agent | Launch sub-agent (Task dispatch with subagent_type) |
| Skill | Execute skill in current session |
| ToolSearch | Load deferred tool schemas |
| ScheduleWakeup | Schedule resume in /loop dynamic mode |

## Deferred (loaded on-demand via ToolSearch)

### User Interaction
- AskUserQuestion - structured option picker (1-4 options, optional preview)
- PushNotification - desktop banner (suppressed when terminal has focus, mobile if Remote Control)

### Plan / Worktree
- EnterPlanMode / ExitPlanMode - native Claude Code plan mode
- EnterWorktree / ExitWorktree - switch git worktrees

### Background Tasks (NOT beads, harness-internal)
- TaskCreate / TaskGet / TaskList / TaskOutput / TaskStop / TaskUpdate - TodoWrite-style harness tracking
- Monitor - stream events from background process
- SendMessage - message to running agent (by name or id)
- TeamCreate / TeamDelete - Agent Teams (used by /lets:team)

### Cron / Scheduled Agents
- CronCreate / CronDelete / CronList - recurring agents (used by /schedule skill)
- RemoteTrigger - trigger remote agent run

### Web
- WebFetch - download URL content
- WebSearch - web search

### Notebook
- NotebookEdit - edit Jupyter .ipynb files

### MCP Resource Discovery (meta)
- ListMcpResourcesTool - enumerate MCP resources
- ReadMcpResourceTool - read specific MCP resource

## Notes for command authors

- Always-loaded tools work without ceremony
- Deferred tools require: ToolSearch -> wait for schema -> call. Common mistake: skipping picker (e.g. AskUserQuestion) because ToolSearch step seems like overhead. DON'T skip - the spec says use it, use it.
- TaskCreate/Get/List family is harness-internal todo tracking, NOT bd. We use bd for cross-session task tracking, not TaskCreate.
- Monitor + run_in_background combo lets you watch long-running processes without blocking.
- Cron* + ScheduleWakeup are different paradigms: ScheduleWakeup wakes the same session later; Cron* spawns separate scheduled agent runs.

## Out of scope (not native)

- MCP server tools (mcp__*) - depend on configured MCP servers (Slack, Google Workspace, context7, ide, playwright)
- LETS plugin commands and skills - separate ecosystem, dispatched via Skill tool

title: Create /lets:remember command - scoped knowledge persistence
description:
## Problem

Knowledge gets lost between sessions or saved to random places. No unified command to persist insights with clear scope choice. Currently:
- bd remember - project-level, shared with team, but not discoverable
- Claude Code auto-memory (MEMORY.md) - user-level, personal, but no interactive flow
- bd comments add - task-level, but only for task context

No single entry point to say 'remember this' with the right scope.

## Solution

/lets:remember command with interactive flow:

### Flow
1. User invokes /lets:remember (optionally with inline text)
2. Discussion phase - Claude helps refine WHAT to remember (too vague? too specific? already saved?)
3. Scope selection via AskUserQuestion:
   - Project (bd remember) - shared knowledge, visible to all team members. Infrastructure facts, architecture decisions, tool quirks, project conventions.
   - User (auto-memory MEMORY.md) - personal preferences, workflow habits, shortcuts. Only visible to this user across sessions.
   - Task (bd comments add) - context for active task. Decisions, findings, blockers specific to current work.
4. Save with confirmation

### Dedup check
Before saving, search existing memories:
- bd memories <keywords> - check project memories
- Read MEMORY.md - check user memories
- If duplicate found, ask: update existing or create new?

### Examples
- 'Remember that dolt push needs reboot after go install' -> Project scope (infra fact)
- 'Remember I prefer Ukrainian for responses' -> User scope (personal pref)
- 'Remember we decided to use labels not epics for grouping' -> Project scope (decision)
- 'Remember the API returns 429 on batch > 100' -> Task scope (finding)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Command with optional inline text argument
- [ ] Discussion phase to refine the insight before saving
- [ ] AskUserQuestion with 3 scope options (project/user/task)
- [ ] Dedup check against existing memories before saving
- [ ] Confirmation after save with what was saved and where
- [ ] Works without active task (task scope disabled if no task)
- [ ] Update hooks/rules-context.md skill reference
- [ ] Update commands/install.md skill tables

title: Add execution mode choice to /lets:execute - here vs team
description:
## Problem

After /lets:plan produces a plan, /lets:execute always runs in current session (native plan mode). If the plan has 5+ independent tasks, /lets:team would be significantly faster. User has no prompt to choose.

## Solution

Before entering plan mode, /lets:execute analyzes the plan and offers execution mode:

### Smart recommendation logic
- < 3 tasks OR sequential dependencies -> 'Execute here (recommended)'
- 3+ independent tasks -> 'Team recommended - N tasks can run in parallel'

### UI
AskUserQuestion with two options:
- Execute here (/lets:execute) - sequential, current session, user approves each step
- Run as team (/lets:team) - parallel, isolated worktrees, faster for independent tasks

### Integration
- /lets:execute reads the plan from .lets/plans/
- Counts tasks, analyzes dependency graph (which tasks depend on others)
- Independent tasks = no dependency between them
- If team recommended but user picks 'here' - proceed normally
- If team selected - hand off to /lets:team with plan reference

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] /lets:execute analyzes plan before entering plan mode
- [ ] AskUserQuestion with execute here vs team option
- [ ] Smart recommendation based on task count and dependencies
- [ ] Seamless handoff to /lets:team when team mode selected
- [ ] Update commands/execute.md
- [ ] Update hooks/rules-context.md skill reference if description changes

title: Split pr.md into separate phase files
description:
## Problem

commands/pr.md is 1196 lines - the largest command file in the plugin. It handles 6 distinct phases with complex state transitions, error recovery, and JSON state management. This is a mini-application in a single markdown file, making it hard to review or modify one phase without affecting others.

## Current phases in one file
1. Analyze - gather PR context, run /lets:review
2. Discuss & Post - interactive discussion, post inline comments
3. Follow-up - check if issues were addressed
4. Approve - approve PR
5. Author Respond - triage and fix review comments
6. Merge/Cancel/Status - state management

## Solution

Split into separate phase files with shared state contract:
- pr.md - entry point, routing, shared state definition
- pr-analyze.md (or inline in pr.md as it's the entry)
- pr-post.md - discuss and post inline comments
- pr-followup.md - follow-up on posted comments
- pr-respond.md - author response flow
- pr-approve.md - approval flow

Shared state via .lets/execution/pr-{number}/ (already exists).

## Scope

Start with pr.md, then audit other large command files for the same problem:
- review.md, brainstorm.md, plan.md, team.md - check line counts and phase complexity
- Any command over ~300 lines with distinct phases is a candidate for splitting

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each phase of pr.md in its own file, independently reviewable
- [ ] Shared state contract documented (JSON schema in pr.md)
- [ ] Entry point routes to correct phase based on flags
- [ ] No behavior changes - pure refactor
- [ ] Audit other large commands and create follow-up tasks if needed
- [ ] Update CLAUDE.md structure section
- [ ] Update plugin.json if commands are registered individually

title: LETS dual-mode: standalone (user scope) + project (git scope)
description:
Split LETS into two modes that coexist in one plugin:

## Problem
LETS requires git + .lets/ + beads for everything. But half the commands (opinion, ask, plan, review, check, brainstorm) don't need a project. User feedback: 'I need lets commands but not bd - just want to quickly work in a random folder.'

## Concept
One plugin, two modes. No explicit switch - each command checks what it needs (capabilities, not modes).

### Standalone mode (no git required)
Works anywhere. Agent commands: opinion, ask, plan, brainstorm, review, check, explore.
State stored in ~/.claude/lets/ (or ~/.lets/ - TBD).
No sessions, no task tracking, no git workflow. Stateless except for plans and config.

### Project mode (git + .lets/)
Full workflow as today. Sessions, commits, tasks, branches, worktrees, teams.
State in <project>/.lets/ as now.

## Architecture decisions (discussed)

### Capability checks instead of mode switch
Each command checks what it needs:
- needs_git() -> git rev-parse || warn
- needs_beads() -> command -v bd || warn  
- needs_lets() -> [ -d .lets/ ] || warn
Command decides what's degradable vs fatal. No global mode flag.

### User scope state location
Options discussed:
- ~/.lets/ - standalone, our own space
- ~/.claude/lets/ - lives with Claude Code config, backup/sync covered
Decision: TBD, needs more thought.

### rules-context.md split
Current: one big rules file injected always.
Proposed: rules-core.md (always) + rules-project.md (only if git + .lets/).
Less noise in standalone = better quality.

### Session identity without git
In standalone: no sessions (stateless). Only agents and plans.
Simplifies ~/.lets/ to just config + plans.

### Plan portability
Plans created in standalone (~/.lets/plans/) don't auto-migrate to project.
User moves manually when needed. /lets:execute searches project .lets/plans/ only.

### Beads in standalone
No beads in standalone. Task tracking is project-only.
Keeps standalone truly lightweight.

## What changes
- Commands get capability checks at start
- SessionStart hook splits rules into core + project
- /lets:install creates ~/.claude/lets/ (user scope) + explains modes
- /lets:init stays project-only
- Agent commands (opinion, ask, plan, etc) work without git
- init.sh gains --skip-beads (already done in lets-wegec)

## Open questions
- ~/.lets/ vs ~/.claude/lets/ for user scope state
- Should /lets:start work in standalone (lightweight, no task)?
- How to handle /lets:plan output location in standalone

comments.author: Dima Slep
comments.text:
Discussion insights from session 2026-03-06:

1. Target users for standalone: (a) dev who uses LETS on main project but opens Claude Code 'just to think', (b) newcomer exploring LETS before committing to a project, (c) non-dev using Claude Code as thinking tool. All valid - capability-based approach covers all.

2. Implicit detection > explicit mode switch. Each command checks capabilities it needs. This is more flexible than binary project/standalone flag. Agreed as core architecture decision.

3. rules-context.md split into core + project reduces context noise in standalone. Agreed, noted for implementation.

4. Plan portability: user moves manually. Keep it simple.

5. User scope location ~/.claude/lets/ vs ~/.lets/ still open. ~/.claude/lets/ has advantage of being inside Claude Code's managed directory.

title: Create /lets:batch command for grouped quick-fix sessions
description:
## Problem

When working on multiple small tasks in a batch (like today's batch-fixes worktree session), the current workflow has friction:

1. **No dedicated command** - user manually picks tasks, switches between them, commits
2. **Premature task closing** - tasks get closed immediately after code change, before commit/review. This loses the link between commit and task closure. Tasks should stay open until /lets:commit or /lets:done finalizes the batch.
3. **No batch overview** - no way to see 'what's in this batch' as a group

## What happened today (reference session)

1. User asked to pick a batch of quick-fix tasks from ready list
2. AI showed all 68 ready tasks, proposed 6 candidates based on priority + estimated effort
3. User approved the batch
4. AI worked through tasks sequentially: read code, make changes, move to next
5. Single commit at the end covering all 6 tasks
6. Problem: AI closed tasks immediately after each code change (bd close) instead of keeping them open until commit

## Proposed /lets:batch command

### Phase 1: Batch Selection
- Show ready tasks grouped by priority (P1 first)
- AI proposes candidates based on: priority, estimated effort (< 30 min each), independence (no deps on each other)
- User approves/adjusts the batch via AskUserQuestion (multiSelect)
- All selected tasks marked in_progress

### Phase 2: Batch Execution
- Work through tasks sequentially
- After each task's code changes: add bd comment with what was done (NOT close)
- Show progress: 'Task 3/6: done. Next: ...'
- Tasks stay in_progress until Phase 3

### Phase 3: Batch Commit & Close
- Triggered by /lets:commit or /lets:done
- Generate single commit message listing all tasks
- Close all batch tasks with reason referencing the commit hash
- Commit footer lists all task IDs

### Key design decisions to make
- Should batch state be persisted to .lets/execution/batch-*.json? (for resume after context loss)
- Should there be a max batch size? (suggest 8-10 tasks)
- How to handle a task that turns out bigger than expected mid-batch? (suggest: skip, create follow-up, or break batch)
- Should /lets:commit auto-detect batch mode from multiple in_progress tasks?
- Commit format: single commit with all tasks, or one commit per task?

## Acceptance criteria
- /lets:batch command with selection, execution, commit phases
- Tasks stay open during work, closed only at commit/done
- bd comments track progress per task (not premature close)
- Batch state persisted for resume
- Progress indicator during execution
- Works in both regular branches and worktrees
- Update Skill Quick Reference in rules-context.md
- Update install.md skill tables

comments.author: Dima Slep
comments.text: Design note: Phase 1 (Batch Selection) should include branch vs worktree choice - same as /lets:start Step 6. After user selects tasks, ask via AskUserQuestion: 'Branch (feature/batch-xxx)' or 'Worktree (.worktrees/batch-xxx)'. This is especially relevant for batch work since it's often done in parallel with main development - worktree is the natural fit. If already in a worktree (like today's session), skip the choice and use current worktree as-is.

title: Research and configure auto-approve for bd and git commands
description:
## Problem

Claude Code asks yes/no permission for every bd and git command execution. This creates friction - dozens of confirmations per session for safe, read-only or routine commands.

## Goal

Minimize permission prompts while keeping safety for destructive operations.

## Research Needed

1. How does Claude Code permission system work?
   - .claude/settings.json allowedTools / blockedTools
   - Per-project vs global settings
   - Regex/glob patterns for command allowlisting
   - "dangerouslyDisableSandbox" implications

2. What can be auto-approved?
   - All bd commands (read-only task tracker)
   - git status, git log, git diff, git branch, git add, git stash
   - gh pr view, gh pr list, gh api (read operations)

3. What should STILL require confirmation?
   - git push, git push --force
   - git reset --hard, git checkout -- (destructive)
   - gh pr merge, gh pr close
   - Any command outside project-root

4. Can we configure this via plugin hooks?
   - PreToolUse hook that auto-approves matching patterns?
   - Or is settings.json the only way?

## Acceptance Criteria

- Document the permission model and configuration options
- Create recommended .claude/settings.json for lets-workflow
- bd commands never prompt
- Safe git commands never prompt
- Destructive git/gh commands still prompt
- Add configuration guidance to /lets:install

title: Add structured memory updates to /lets:end
description:
## Context

Claude sometimes writes to MEMORY.md during sessions ("update memory with session lessons"). This happens ad-hoc, inconsistently, and sometimes spams low-value stuff.

## Idea

Add a memory review step to /lets:end (or a separate /lets:remember command):

1. At session end, Claude reviews what happened in the session
2. Identifies stable patterns/lessons worth remembering (not session-specific noise)
3. Shows proposed memory updates to user via AskUserQuestion:
   - "Save to memory" / "Skip" / "Edit" per item
4. Writes approved items to MEMORY.md

## What qualifies for memory

- Confirmed patterns across multiple interactions
- Infrastructure facts (URLs, passwords, configs)
- Workflow preferences the user stated
- Tool/command gotchas discovered (like --notes vs bd comments add)
- Architecture decisions

## What does NOT qualify

- Session-specific context (current task, in-progress work)
- Single-occurrence observations not yet verified
- Anything already in CLAUDE.md or rules-context.md

## Anti-spam rules

- Max 2-3 items per session
- Don't duplicate existing memory entries - check first
- Don't write speculative conclusions
- User approves every write

## Acceptance Criteria

- /lets:end has optional memory review step (skippable, especially in --fast mode)
- Proposed items shown with AskUserQuestion
- Only user-approved items written
- Existing entries checked for duplicates before proposing
- Memory stays concise (MEMORY.md < 200 lines as per system rules)
close_reason: Merged into lets-wwh2l (Enhance /lets:end)

title: Integrate beads molecules into plan/execute/team workflow
description:
## Context

Beads has "molecules" - epics with workflow semantics. Children parallel by default, explicit deps create sequence. Commands: bd mol pour (template->instance), bd mol wisp (ephemeral), bd mol bond (connect graphs), bd mol squash/burn (cleanup).

See: https://github.com/steveyegge/beads/blob/main/docs/MOLECULES.md

## Opportunity

Replace manual step tracking in our skills with molecule-based execution:

### /lets:execute
Currently: reads plan file, tracks step index manually, sequential by default.
With molecules: plan steps become molecule children with deps. bd ready shows what's executable. Parallel steps run in parallel naturally. No manual step tracking.

### /lets:team
Currently: creates tasks manually, assigns to agents.
With molecules: bd mol pour creates the work graph. Agents claim bd ready work. Dependencies auto-gate. Bond discovered work at runtime.

### /lets:plan (from lets-mp5v5)
Currently: outputs markdown plan file.
With molecules: output a molecule template. bd mol pour to instantiate for execution. Reusable templates for common patterns.

### /lets:brainstorm
Could store plan as molecule prototype for later pour.

## Key Benefits

- Parallel-by-default matches real work (most steps ARE independent)
- No manual step tracking - bd ready/blocked handles it
- Work graph visible via bd show/bd blocked
- Agents can bond discovered work without disrupting flow
- Squash/burn for cleanup after execution

## Acceptance Criteria

- /lets:execute uses molecules for step tracking
- Plan output from /lets:plan is molecule-compatible
- /lets:team leverages molecule graph for agent dispatch
- Existing bd ready/blocked/close workflow unchanged
- Migration path from current plan files
notes: bd swarm command available since v0.58.0: bd swarm create/list/status/validate. Creates swarm molecule from epic. Check bd swarm --help for details.

title: Add theme-by-theme spec review format to review/brainstorm/plan skills
description:
## Format: Theme-by-Theme Spec Review

Reviewer reads a spec/plan/document and raises concrete themes for discussion - one at a time. Each theme has:
- **Name**: short topic label
- **Context**: what the spec says now
- **Problem**: why this is a question
- **Options**: solutions with trade-offs (table or list)

Author picks an option or proposes their own. Decisions are recorded immediately (beads notes or plan file).

Benefits:
- Systematic walk-through, nothing missed
- Incremental decisions instead of "read 900 lines and give feedback"
- Each theme is self-contained and actionable

## Where to Apply

### /lets:review --spec (or --plan)
- Review implementation plans or spec documents theme-by-theme
- Agent reads the document, extracts themes, presents one by one via AskUserQuestion
- Decisions saved to task notes

### /lets:brainstorm
- After generating options/architecture, present each design decision as a theme
- Instead of dumping full plan at once, walk through theme by theme
- Natural fit for the clarification phase

### /lets:plan (from lets-mp5v5)
- Plan review before execution: walk through plan themes for user approval
- Each architectural decision = one theme with trade-offs
- Approved decisions go into the final plan file

## Acceptance Criteria

- Theme-by-theme format documented as a reusable pattern
- At least one skill implements it (most likely /lets:review --spec or /lets:brainstorm)
- AskUserQuestion per theme with options + "Other" for custom input
- Decisions recorded to beads task notes or plan file

title: Add 'Merge & close' option to /lets:done post-PR menu
description:
## Problem

After /lets:done creates a PR (github: true mode), the "What's next?" menu offers: Stay on branch, Next task, End session, Type something, Chat. But there's no option to immediately merge the PR and close the task - which is the most common next step for small/obvious PRs.

User has to manually run /lets:pr --merge or go to GitHub.

## Solution

Add option to the AskUserQuestion after PR creation:

```
Task done. What's next?

1. Merge & close       <- NEW
   Merge PR #{number}, close task, switch to main
2. Stay on branch
   Stay on feature branch - for PR fixes or follow-up work
3. Next task
   Switch to main, pick another task
4. End session
   Switch to main, run /lets:end
```

"Merge & close" should:
1. gh pr merge <number> --squash (or --merge based on repo settings)
2. bd close <task-id>
3. Switch to main, pull
4. Clean up feature branch

## Acceptance Criteria

- New option appears first in the menu (most common action)
- Uses gh pr merge with appropriate strategy
- Closes beads task after successful merge
- Switches to main and cleans up branch
- Handles merge conflicts gracefully (fall back to "Stay on branch")

title: Create /lets:discuss - interactive expert panel via Agent Teams
description:
## Feature
New command for interactive multi-expert discussions using Agent Teams (no worktree).

## Position in skill spectrum
- /lets:ask - 1 expert, 1 question, fire-and-forget (Slack ping)
- /lets:opinion - 3-5 experts, parallel, fire-and-forget (async poll)
- /lets:discuss - N experts, interactive, follow-ups (meeting)

## How it works
1. User describes topic/question
2. Select experts (same catalog as opinion)
3. TeamCreate + spawn experts as teammates (NO worktree, read-only agents)
4. Experts analyze and respond
5. Lead (user) can:
   - Ask follow-up to specific expert
   - Ask one expert to respond to another's finding
   - Request deeper analysis on specific point
   - Steer the discussion
6. When satisfied: shutdown team, summarize findings

## Key design decisions
- Uses Agent Teams (TeamCreate/Agent/SendMessage) NOT Task() subagents
- No worktree isolation (read-only experts don't write code)
- Experts use existing lets:* agent types (architect, security-expert, etc.)
- mode: plan NOT needed (read-only, no edits to approve)
- Team lead is the main Claude session

## Integration with /lets:brainstorm
Step 7 (Expert Evaluation) could delegate to /lets:discuss instead of Task() fire-and-forget.
This makes evaluation interactive without changing brainstorm's structure.

## Depends on
- lets-elhe6 (--worktree flag) conceptually related but can be built independently
- /lets:team exists as reference implementation for Agent Teams pattern

## Output
Summary of discussion + key findings, saved to beads comment on active task.

title: Add --worktree flag to /lets:team for optional isolation
description:
## Feature
Make worktree isolation optional in /lets:team via --worktree flag.

## Current behavior
team.md always passes isolation: worktree to Agent() - teammates always get isolated worktrees.

## Proposed behavior
- /lets:team run - no worktree isolation (teammates work in same repo, read-only use cases)
- /lets:team run --worktree - with worktree isolation (implementation, code changes)

## Use cases
- Without worktree: expert evaluation teams (brainstorm Step 7 replacement), parallel analysis, discussion teams
- With worktree: parallel implementation (current behavior)

## Key integration: /lets:brainstorm Step 7 (Expert Evaluation)
Currently Step 7 uses Task() fire-and-forget subagents for evaluation. With --worktree flag:
- brainstorm Step 7 could use /lets:team run (no worktree) for interactive expert evaluation
- Lead can ask follow-up questions to specific experts
- Experts can be asked to revise their evaluation after seeing other findings
- Lead can reject an evaluation and ask expert to dig deeper
- This turns evaluation from fire-and-forget into a conversation with experts

Flow: brainstorm reaches Step 7 -> /lets:team run with selected experts -> interactive evaluation -> shutdown team -> brainstorm continues to Step 8

## Implementation notes
- isolation: worktree is an optional param on Agent() - just omit it for no-worktree mode
- Without worktree, auto cherry-pick behavior doesn't apply (no separate branches)
- Without worktree, teammates share the working directory - conflicts possible if multiple write
- Consider: no-worktree mode should default to read-only agents, worktree mode to implementer
- Update teammate prompt template for both modes
- Update completion flow (no branch discovery needed in either mode, but commit verification differs)

## Opens up
- /lets:brainstorm Step 7 interactive expert evaluation (main motivation)
- /lets:review could offer team mode for deep reviews with follow-up questions
- Any command that dispatches multiple experts could use team mode for interactivity
close_reason: Merged into lets-csc1o (Polish /lets:team v2)

title: Add --fast flag to /lets:end for quick session close
description:
## Problem

When context is at 0% or near-zero, /lets:end often fails or is too slow because it tries to generate a full summary. User frequently writes "/lets:end тільки швидко контекста нуль" to force a quick close.

## Solution

Add --fast flag to /lets:end that:
- Skips summary generation (or writes minimal 2-3 line summary)
- Skips beads sync if it would be slow
- Just saves session ref, marks task status, exits
- Basically: git status + session-start-ref update + done

## When to Auto-detect

Consider auto-triggering fast mode when context is critically low (< 5%), since there's not enough context to generate a meaningful summary anyway.

## Acceptance Criteria

- /lets:end --fast closes session in under 5 seconds
- Writes minimal summary (timestamp, branch, task-id, "fast close - no summary")
- Session ref saved so next /lets:start knows where to resume
- Works even at 0% context remaining

title: Fix session summary handling in worktrees
description:
## Problem

last-summary.md in .lets/sessions/ is shared between main repo and worktrees (via symlink). When a worktree session ends, it overwrites the main repo's last summary. Multiple parallel worktrees overwrite each other.

## Options

Option A: Timestamped summaries with worktree label
- Don't write last-summary.md from worktrees at all
- Instead write: summary-{timestamp}-worktree-{name}.md
- Main repo keeps using last-summary.md as before
- /lets:start reads last-summary.md OR finds latest summary-*.md matching current context

Option B: Branch-specific last summaries
- last-summary-{branch}.md per branch
- /lets:start reads the one matching current branch

Option A seems simpler and avoids conflicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parallel worktree sessions don't overwrite each other's summaries
- Main repo summary isn't overwritten by worktree sessions
- /lets:start can still restore context from the right summary
- Old last-summary.md flow unchanged for non-worktree sessions

## Research: tmux + VS Code integration (2026-03-25)

VS Code extensions: Tmux Keybinding (9K installs, tmux-style keys), vscode-tmux-manager (1K, tree view sidebar).

Persistent terminal profile pattern:
  path: tmux, args: [new-session, -A, -s, vscode:${workspaceFolder}]

- claude-tmux (Rust TUI) - multi-session dashboard with status/preview

title: lets:pr should not switch branches in worktree
description:

Fix: detect worktree context in /lets:pr and skip branch checkout. Use gh pr diff exclusively.

title: Add user confirmation gates to /lets:pr flow
description:
## Problem

/lets:pr flow jumps between phases without user confirmation:
- After Phase 1 (review analysis) -> immediately transitions to Phase 2 (discuss findings) with no pause
- Line 262 in pr.md: "Transition to Phase 2 immediately (no need for separate invocation)"
- User has no chance to review the summary, read the JSON, or decide whether to proceed

## Expected Behavior

Every phase transition should have an AskUserQuestion gate with options to:
- Continue to next phase
- Skip phase (e.g., skip discussion, post all as-is)
- Save and exit (resume later with `/lets:pr`)
- Cancel review entirely

## Specific Gates to Add

1. **After Phase 1 summary (2.5)** - before entering Phase 2 discussion:
   - "Continue to discuss findings?" / "Post all without discussion" / "Save for later" / "Cancel"

2. **Review Phase 2 finding-by-finding flow** - already has AskUserQuestion per finding (good), but add:
   - Batch option: "Apply same disposition to remaining {N} findings" when pattern emerges
   
3. **Verify Phase 3 (follow-up) and Phase 4 (approve) also have gates** - audit all phase transitions

## Acceptance Criteria

- No phase transition happens without user confirmation
- Every gate has a "save for later" option (leverages existing state file)
- Every gate has a "skip"/"cancel" option
- Finding-by-finding discussion has batch shortcut for remaining items

title: Fix setup-beads-remote.sh SSH/HTTPS protocol detection

- Script detects git protocol (ssh vs https) and uses correct remote URL format
- Script starts dolt sql-server before bd init if not already running
- Script works out of the box for both SSH and HTTPS auth setups

## Plan rejection test 2026-03-02

### CRITICAL FINDING: mode: plan did NOT enforce plan approval

Spawned teammate with mode: 'plan' but teammate bypassed it entirely:
- No plan_approval_request received by lead
- Teammate directly edited files and committed
- Task completed without any plan review

### Impact
plan_mode_required was supposed to be the key security enforcement mechanism.
Without it, teammates can make arbitrary changes in their worktrees.

### Possible causes
1. mode: 'plan' may not work with custom agent types (lets:implementer)
2. haiku model may not respect plan mode constraints
3. mode parameter may require different syntax or additional config

### Action needed
- Investigate how mode: 'plan' actually works in Agent Teams
- Test with mode: 'plan' on general-purpose agent type
- If mode: plan is unreliable: consider alternative enforcement (PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write)
- Create separate bug task

### Note
First smoke test DID get plan_approval_requests (both teammates). Difference: same model (haiku), same mode. May be intermittent.

comments.author: Dima Slep
comments.text:
## Plan rejection test 2026-03-02

### Result: PARTIAL SUCCESS

With full teammate prompt template (PLAN FIRST section), sonnet:
1. Teammate sent plan_approval_request - OK
2. Lead rejected with specific feedback - OK
3. Teammate did NOT resubmit revised plan - just implemented directly
4. BUT: teammate DID follow the rejection feedback in the actual code
   - Renamed section from 'Usage Example' to 'Note' (as requested)
   - Removed Agent() call (as requested)
   - Kept it short (as requested)
5. Teammate's completion MESSAGE still said old plan ('Usage Example') - stale text

### Conclusion
Plan rejection delivers feedback and teammate uses it, but doesn't force a second plan approval cycle. After rejection, teammate goes straight to implementation with revised approach. This is acceptable behavior for v1 - feedback is applied, just without a second review gate.

### mode: plan summary (all tests)
- Full prompt + mode: plan -> plan approval works (smoke test 1, rejection test)
- Minimal prompt + mode: plan -> bypassed (haiku AND sonnet)
- Plan rejection -> feedback applied but no re-approval cycle
- Enforcement is 100% prompt-driven, mode: plan is just a hint

title: bd dolt push/pull timeout: MySQL client readTimeout too short for git remote operations
description:
## Problem

bd dolt push and bd dolt pull always fail with 'invalid connection' when using git+https remote (e.g. GitHub).

The operations actually complete successfully on the dolt server side, but bd client disconnects before getting a response.

## Root Cause

In internal/storage/dolt/store.go:646, buildServerDSN sets:
```go
params := "parseTime=true&timeout=5s&readTimeout=10s&writeTimeout=10s"
```

readTimeout=10s and writeTimeout=10s are too short for remote operations. A dolt push to git+https://github.com remote takes 30-90 seconds (git fetch + upload). The MySQL connection times out at 10s, bd reports 'invalid connection', but the server completes the push successfully.

## Evidence

- `bd dolt push` -> `[mysql] packets.go:58 read tcp 127.0.0.1:XXXXX->127.0.0.1:13771: i/o timeout`
- Server log shows no errors, connection lives for 30-40 seconds
- Direct `cd .beads/dolt/lets && dolt push origin main` works fine (takes ~90 sec)
- `git ls-remote` confirms data was pushed despite bd reporting failure
- auto-push warnings appear on every bd command because of this

## Environment
- bd 0.56.1
- dolt 1.82.6
- Remote: git+https://github.com (private repo)
- macOS

## Suggested Fix

Use a longer timeout (or no timeout) for remote operations (push/pull). Regular queries are fast and benefit from 10s timeout, but remote ops need 2-5 minutes. Options:
1. Separate DSN for remote operations with longer timeouts
2. Remove readTimeout/writeTimeout from remote op connections
3. Make timeout configurable via config.yaml

title: Optimize /lets:start with quick modes and task argument
description:
Currently /lets:start always runs full cycle: last-summary + git state + bd ready (full list) + task selection question. This is overhead when user already knows what to work on.

## Proposed modes

### 1. /lets:start <task-id> - quick start with specific task
- Skip bd ready and task selection
- Show only bd show <task-id> + comments (task context)
- Create/switch branch immediately
- Much faster for known work

### 2. /lets:start (no args) - full flow as today
- Last session summary
- Git state
- bd ready list
- Task selection question

### 3. /lets:start --continue - resume last in_progress task
- Find last in_progress task automatically
- Skip selection, go straight to branch
- Good for multi-session tasks

### 4. /lets:start --quick - minimal output
- Skip last-summary, skip full bd ready
- Just git state + task selection (compact)

## Open questions
- How to pass arguments to skills in Claude Code? Need to verify syntax
- Should full bd ready be lazy-loaded (only if user asks)?
- Can we detect if there's an obvious next task (only 1 in_progress) and auto-suggest?

## Acceptance criteria
- /lets:start with task ID skips selection and goes straight to branch
- /lets:start without args works as before (backwards compatible)
- At least one quick mode implemented
- Context recovery (bd show + comments) works in quick mode

title: Enforce project-root boundary for agents and subagents
description:
Agents and subagents sometimes escape project-root - reading network volumes, Downloads folder, parent directories. This triggers macOS permission dialogs and is a security/privacy concern.

## Problem
- rules-context.md has the rule but it's text-only - agents can ignore it
- Subagents launched by /lets:review, /lets:opinion etc. don't always respect boundaries
- macOS shows permission popups when Claude tries to access network volumes or system folders

## What to investigate
- Can we use hooks (PreToolUse) to block Read/Glob/Grep calls outside project-root?
- Can we pass project-root constraint to subagents more explicitly?
- Are there Claude Code settings that restrict file access scope?

## Acceptance criteria
- No file access outside project-root unless user explicitly requests it
- Subagents respect the same boundary
- No macOS permission popups during normal workflow

title: Add memory/task capture check to /lets:end
description:
Before ending session, /lets:end should prompt to capture insights:

1. Check if anything discussed should be saved to memory (workflow patterns, user preferences, architectural decisions)
2. Check if any new tasks/improvements were identified during the session but not yet tracked in beads
3. Check active task - prompt to add notes/comments before closing (often you work on a task, discover something important but don't record it, then close the session and lose context)
4. Ask user: 'Anything to remember or track from this session?'

This prevents losing valuable context that came up organically during work.

Acceptance criteria:
- New step in end.md between Step 4 (task status) and Step 5 (session summary)
- Prompts user about untracked insights/tasks
- Checks memory files for anything to update
- Reminds to add notes to active task before closing

title: Remove yaml->env migration code from session-start.sh after universal migration
description:
The auto-migration block in hooks/session-start.sh (lines ~17-72) converts legacy .lets/config.yaml to .lets/.env on first session.

It runs on every session start (idempotent gate), but only performs work if .env is missing AND yaml exists. After all known users have migrated, this code is dead weight.

## Trigger

Remove when: all known projects have .lets/.env on disk (no surviving config.yaml without matching .env). Sanity check by polling known users.

## Scope

- Delete migration block in hooks/session-start.sh (~50 lines: mkdir guard, parser, mktemp/atomic write, LETS Notice emit)
- Delete the legacy notice in scripts/lets/init.sh (~3 lines)
- Update CLAUDE.md 'User config file' section to remove migration mention
- Update README.md migration notice to remove
- Update hooks/rules-context.md 'auto-created on first session if .lets/config.yaml exists' to drop legacy reference

## Why

SessionStart hook responsibility: emit context for the model. yaml parsing + atomic file writes are a different responsibility hitched along for one-time convenience. Acceptable now (do once, do right) but should not live forever (SRP).

title: Track upstream #55648 — restore agent memory when Anthropic fixes the bug
description:
## Context

We disabled `memory: project` for all 14 LETS agents as a workaround for upstream Claude Code bug: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/55648

Bug summary: subagents with `memory: project` frontmatter skip assigned tasks when writing memory, returning only memory-write confirmation. Affects /lets:review, /lets:plan, /lets:opinion, /lets:brainstorm dispatchers.

## What we had before disable

Per-agent memory enabled via frontmatter:
```yaml
memory: project
```

This created per-agent memory directories at `.claude/agent-memory/lets-<agent>/` per project, with auto-managed MEMORY.md index + individual memory files.

Each agent file had:
- `## Memory (after output)` section explaining what to persist
- `Remember:` bullets (domain-specific knowledge categories)
- `Do NOT remember:` bullets (anti-patterns)
- Opener: 'After your text response, persist project-specific {domain} knowledge for future sessions. Memory is an addition, not a replacement for your text response.'

PRs that introduced and tightened this:
- PR #43: Renamed Memory Guidance -> Memory (after output), added subordination opener
- PR #44: Added MANDATORY block in Output Format sections, refined opener wording

Each orchestrator command (commands/review.md, plan.md, opinion.md) had MANDATORY clauses in Task templates instructing agents to emit response BEFORE memory writes.

## What to watch (signals to re-evaluate)

Upstream channels:
- Issue #55648 status — comments, label changes, fix commits
- Anthropic Claude Code release notes for memory: project changes (v2.1.130+ likely)
- Related: #50677 (memory bias), #44829 (autoMemoryEnabled suppress), #52706 (confirmation gate), #39496 (opt-in memory), #54208 (memory path bug)

Look for:
- New `memory: <value>` values like `disabled`, `read_only`, `opt-in`
- Per-Task override flag in Task tool API
- Hook events PreMemoryWrite / PostMemoryWrite (#44820)
- `autoMemoryEnabled: false` actually suppressing system prompt injection

## How to restore (if/when fixed)

If Anthropic adds opt-in/opt-out mechanism:
1. Add `memory: <new-value>` to relevant agent frontmatter (likely 12-14 agents — re-evaluate scope based on what fix provides)
2. Restore `## Memory (after output)` sections (template in git history pre-disable)
3. Restore MANDATORY blocks if needed (template in pre-disable PRs #43, #44)
4. Re-test with /lets:review on real plan to verify no regression

If Anthropic doesn't fix:
- Stay on workaround indefinitely
- Consider architectural alternative: orchestrator-managed memory (main agent writes per-agent files based on subagent findings, with user curation)

## Empirical findings reference

5-agent dispatch variance pre-disable (compliance with structured OUTPUT FORMAT):
- qa: full
- architect: partial
- security: partial
- pragmatist: stub
- backend: memory-only

Test-agent reproduction: minimal agent file with only `memory: project` frontmatter (no body memory mentions) reliably triggered substitution given forward-looking prompt context.

Workaround verification: same agent file without `memory: project` produces full structured response.

## When to revisit

Quarterly check, or sooner if:
- Issue #55648 gets active triage from Anthropic
- Claude Code release notes mention memory: project changes
- Community workarounds emerge (e.g. hook-based memory blocking)

title: bd v0.62.0 to v1.0.2 upgrade: fix legacy dolt remote causing slow commands in shared-server mode
description:
Problem: After upgrading bd from v0.62.0 to v1.0.2 locally (built from source, tag v1.0.2), all bd commands against the shared VPS Dolt server became extremely slow. First bd ready took 7m52s. Subsequent commands 18-54s.

Root cause:
bd 1.0.2 on every store open calls syncCLIRemotesToSQL (internal/storage/dolt/store.go:1138, GH#2315). It reads legacy CLI-level remotes from .beads/dolt/lets/.dolt/repo_state.json (leftover from embedded-dolt era before migration to shared VPS server on 2026-03-09) and re-registers them in the SQL server via CALL DOLT_REMOTE(add, ?, ?). Our shared-user Jkd5sgUq90 has no permission for that procedure, so every call gets command denied and bd wastes time on each retry.

Secondary: bd 1.0.x also attempts CALL DOLT_BACKUP(rm/add) via auto-backup, but this was already disabled by lead via backup.enabled: false in .beads/config.yaml (yaml is read correctly - my earlier assumption was wrong).

Fix applied:
cd .beads/dolt/lets && dolt remote rm origin

This clears the legacy origin remote (git+ssh://git@github.com/restarter/lets-workflow-beads.git) from repo_state.json. Since migration to Direct SQL mode against VPS, .beads/dolt/lets/ is unused but still read by bd for CLI remote sync. With remote gone, syncCLIRemotesToSQL has nothing to propagate.

Verification:
- bd stats: 22s (was 18s before fix, but with DOLT_REMOTE errors)
- bd list closed limit 5: 14s
- bd show lets-6xe7b: 12s
- VPS dolt logs: zero DOLT_REMOTE / DOLT_BACKUP permission denied errors after fix
- Only remaining warning: nothing to commit from benign auto-commit checks

Caveat:
Remaining ~12-22s overhead per read command is cost of shared-server mode in bd 1.0.x (auto-commit checks, multiple connection open/close). In v0.62.0 was sub-second. Not perfect but usable.

Additional findings:
- Dolt VPS version: 1.83.0 (pinned in /opt/dolt-remote/.env)
- Schema on VPS still at pre-v1.0.0 (no custom_statuses / custom_types tables)
- bd 1.0.2 can read pre-v1.0 schema via SQL; no forced migration on read-only commands
- bd was built locally from source at beads-work/beads (tag v1.0.2) via make install-force

Upstream impact:
This affects anyone who migrated embedded Dolt to shared-server mode before upgrading to 1.0.x. Worth reporting to gastownhall/beads. syncCLIRemotesToSQL should be skipped when DoltMode == server (client has no CLI data dir to sync from in that case anyway).

comments.author: Artem Shybko
comments.text:
ADDITIONAL FINDING (same session, 2026-04-24): export.auto N+1 bug

After fixing the legacy dolt remote, bd read commands worked at ~20s but writes (create/close) were still extremely slow - 8 minutes for bd create, 32s for bd close.

Root cause identified via upstream issues:
- gastownhall/beads#3414 (OPEN) - "auto-export hydrate-labels query times out (~10-15s, context canceled) on Dolt remote backend" - exact match for our symptoms on bd 1.0.2 + remote Dolt.
- gastownhall/beads#3239 (OPEN) - "Batch wisp routing checks to reduce WAN latency amplification in Dolt server mode" - related N+1 pattern in IsActiveWispInTx loop.

Both are N+1 query bugs amplified by WAN latency. Every mutating bd command runs maybeAutoExport in PersistentPostRun, which hydrates labels per issue. Over remote SQL each round-trip adds up exponentially. On our 173-issue DB this took 8 minutes on bd create.

Workaround (from #3414):
bd config set export.auto false

After applying:
- bd create: 8 minutes -> 33 seconds (15x faster)
- bd close: 32s -> 33s (no change, close was not the bottleneck)
- bd stats/show (reads): 12-20s unchanged

Trade-off: .beads/issues.jsonl no longer auto-updates after writes. Not a problem for us since .beads/ is gitignored and the JSONL is never committed.

Updated .beads/config.yaml now contains three keys:
- backup.enabled: false (lead, March, disables JSONL backup)
- dolt.auto-push: false (lead, March, disables auto-push)
- export.auto: false (this session, April, disables slow hydrate-labels auto-export)

Both upstream issues are OPEN without maintainer response - worth signalling impact via comments there.

comments.author: Artem Shybko
comments.text:
## Session End 2026-04-24 23:00 - final summary

Complete picture after full investigation:

### Two distinct fixes were needed (not one)

**Fix 1** - legacy dolt remote:
cd .beads/dolt/lets && dolt remote rm origin
(Removes origin remote left over from embedded-dolt era. bd 1.0.2 syncCLIRemotesToSQL re-registers it every command -> permission denied on shared user.)

**Fix 2** - disable auto-export (the big one):
echo "export.auto: false" >> .beads/config.yaml
(N+1 hydrate-labels query during maybeAutoExport - 8 minute bd create without this.)

### Performance impact after both fixes

- bd create: 8 min -> 33 seconds (15x)
- bd close/delete/comment: 27-33 sec (unchanged, was already acceptable)
- bd stats/show/list: 18-22 sec (unchanged, WAN latency limit)

### Data integrity confirmed

Initial panic about data divergence was WRONG. Caused by misleading dolt sql -q behavior inside docker container - it queries committed main branch (only initial commit exists) while real data lives in sql-server working set. Direct MySQL wire protocol query confirms:
- VPS lets DB: 175 issues, all synced, no data loss
- bd stats matches MySQL count exactly
- beads-web panel shows all data correctly after UI filter adjustment

Lesson: verify dolt data via MySQL protocol on port 3306, not dolt sql -q inside container.

### Upstream status

Both workarounds correspond to OPEN upstream issues:
- gastownhall/beads#3414 - auto-export hydrate timeout (exact match)
- gastownhall/beads#3239 - WAN latency amplification from N+1 queries

No maintainer response on either. Affects all shared-server mode users on bd 1.0.x.

### Applied to all projects

Both lets-workflow and aff.local now have identical config.yaml workarounds:
- backup.enabled: false
- dolt.auto-push: false
- export.auto: false

aff.local did not need Fix 1 (never had embedded mode).

### Artefacts

- Local bd: 1.0.2 at ~/.local/bin/bd (backup ~/.local/bin/bd-0.62.0)
- beads-work/beads: detached HEAD at v1.0.2 tag
- Session file: .lets/sessions/2026-04-24-2300-main.md

title: Design .gitignore strategy for .lets/ folder
description:
Currently .lets/ is fully gitignored (entry '.lets/' in root .gitignore). Need to think through which subfolders/files should actually be tracked and which should stay ignored.

Context: .lets/ is created by /lets:init and contains mixed content:

    config.yaml          # per-project settings (language, merge-branch, github) - potentially team-shared
    config.example.yaml  # template with defaults
    statusline.sh        # copied from scripts/lets/statusline.sh - regenerated on /lets:init
    sessions/            # session summaries, session-start-ref - per-developer, ephemeral
    reviews/             # saved review reports - per-developer, can be large
    plans/               # implementation plans - potentially shareable
    execution/           # execution state (pr-N/, team-*.json) - ephemeral
    cache/               # usage stats, internal data - gitignored for sure
    backups/             # (currently only in lets-workflow) - ephemeral
    _config local.yaml   # (currently only in lets-workflow) - personal override

Questions to decide:
- Should config.yaml be shared (team-consistent language/merge-branch) or per-developer?
- Should plans/ be shared (collaborative planning) or per-developer?
- If some are shared, strategy: create .lets/.gitignore with inverse rules (!config.yaml, cache/, etc) OR change root .gitignore to be more granular
- How does this interact with backups/ folder (where does it come from, is it beads-generated)?
- Review /lets:init script to ensure it generates consistent structure

Deliverable: decision on what to track + update init.sh to create .lets/.gitignore (or root-level granular rules).

title: Study gstack patterns and adapt for LETS
description:
Reference repo garrytan/gstack cloned to reference/gstack/. Garry Tan's 28-skill Claude Code workflow that enforces Think->Plan->Build->Review->Test->Ship->Reflect sprint cycle.

Key ideas to evaluate and potentially adapt:
1. Documentation as code - SKILL.md auto-generated from templates (SKILL.md.tmpl + gen-skill-docs.ts). Our docs drift manually.
2. Explicit exit criteria per skill/command - each phase has formal 'done' conditions. We lack this.
3. Progressive safety levels (/careful, /freeze, /guard) instead of binary on/off. Our agents have read-only constraints but no levels.
4. Role-based reasoning throughout workflow - not just for dispatched opinions but for every phase.
5. Multi-platform setup script - single installer for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kiro, Gemini CLI.

Start by reading ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md, and 3-4 key skills (office-hours, review, qa, ship) to extract actionable patterns.

title: Add PreToolUse hooks for enforcing plugin workflow conventions
description:
## Problem

Plugin has conventions that models can bypass: direct bd create without skill, agents writing files when they should be read-only, etc. Rules in rules-context.md are soft - model can ignore them.

## Solution

PreToolUse hooks using prompt-based and command-based types to enforce plugin conventions. Prompt hooks (type: prompt) for soft enforcement - LLM evaluates and provides feedback. Command hooks (type: command) for hard enforcement where needed.

## Hook Implementation Plan

### Hook 1: bd create enforcement (prompt hook)
- Event: PreToolUse, matcher: Bash
- Type: prompt - evaluate if command contains bd create outside of skill context
- Action: deny with reason "Use /lets:create-task skill instead of direct bd create"
- Recursive handling: prompt should be aware that skill itself calls bd create legitimately

### Hook 2: Read-only agent enforcement (command hook)
- Event: PreToolUse, matcher: Edit|Write
- Type: command - check if running inside a read-only agent context
- Action: exit 2 (block) with stderr feedback
- Prototype exists: hooks/validate-readonly.sh.old
- Challenge: detecting agent context from hook stdin (SubagentStart may help)

### Hook 3: Direct git commit prevention (prompt hook)
- Event: PreToolUse, matcher: Bash
- Type: prompt - evaluate if command is git commit (not from /lets:commit skill)
- Action: deny with reason "Use /lets:commit for proper task linking and review"

### Hook 4: Project boundary warning (prompt hook)
- Event: PreToolUse, matcher: Read|Grep|Glob
- Type: prompt - check if target path is outside project-root
- Action: deny with reason explaining boundary

## Hook Types Reference

- type: command - shell script, exit 0/2, fast
- type: prompt - single LLM call (Haiku), returns ok/reason, good for judgment
- type: agent - subagent with tools, for verification requiring file inspection
- type: http - POST to endpoint, for audit/logging

## Registration

All hooks registered in hooks/hooks.json (already exists in plugin).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Rule added to rules-context.md for bd create (path A, immediate)
- [ ] PreToolUse prompt hook for bd create detection
- [ ] Hook handles recursive skill context
- [ ] Evaluate validate-readonly.sh.old for reuse with command hook type
- [ ] PreToolUse prompt hook for git commit detection
- [ ] Document hook patterns for future enforcement
- [ ] Test all hooks dont break normal workflow

comments.author: Dima Slep
comments.text:
Research from hooks-guide (2026-03-18):

NEW HOOK TYPES available (beyond command):
- type: prompt - LLM-based (Haiku default, configurable model). Returns ok/reason JSON. Perfect for soft enforcement - model evaluates and self-corrects.
- type: agent - subagent with tool access (Read, Grep, etc). Up to 50 tool turns, 60s default timeout. For verification requiring codebase inspection.
- type: http - POST to HTTP endpoint. For team-wide audit/logging.

KEY EVENTS for our use cases:
- PreToolUse (matcher: Bash|Edit|Write) - intercept before execution, can deny/allow/ask
- SubagentStart - could enforce agent constraints at spawn time
- WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove - proper worktree lifecycle hooks
- InstructionsLoaded - when CLAUDE.md loads, could inject dynamic rules
- Stop - verify task completion before allowing stop

DESIGN INSIGHTS:
- prompt hooks are ideal for soft enforcement (remind, not block) - exactly what we need
- PreToolUse can return permissionDecision: deny with reason - Claude gets feedback
- Matcher is regex on tool name, not command content - for Bash content inspection need to parse tool_input.command in the hook
- Exit 2 = block with stderr feedback to Claude
- Hooks run in parallel, deduplicated
- Plugin hooks go in hooks/hooks.json (already have this file)
- Skill/agent frontmatter hooks also supported but we found they were silently ignored before

comments.text:
## Reconsidered 2026-05-03

Demoted from P1 to P3. Reason for cooling on this task:

### Concerns

1. **Friction cost > enforcement value**: prompt hooks require Haiku LLM call on EVERY Bash/Edit/Write tool call. False positives unavoidable, latency added, recursive context handling (skill calls bd create legitimately) is non-trivial.

2. **Hook 2 already solved structurally**: PR #48 (lets-72v34, 2026-05-03) removed Edit/Write from all 13 analyst agents. Read-only constraint is structural, hook would be duplicate enforcement.

3. **Soft enforcement now stronger**: lets-xjydz (this session, c0b2070+a46e455) added PreCompact hook so workflow rules from rules-context.md persist across compaction. Soft enforcement via documented rules is more reliable than before.

4. **Bd create / git commit hooks**: would block legitimate ad-hoc usage. The skills (create-task, commit) are guidance, not strict gates - using bd create directly for one-off cases is fine.

5. **Stale references in original spec**: validate-readonly.sh.old no longer exists in repo (was a prototype that never registered). Hook 4 (project boundary) had no concrete use case.

### What replaces it

- rules-context.md as source of truth for conventions
- Structural removal of tools where possible (Write from analysts)
- PreCompact ensures rules survive long sessions
- /lets:* commands as encouraged (not enforced) entry points

Keeping open at P3 in case we revisit specific hooks in future (e.g. if recursive bd create becomes a real problem).

comments.author: Dima Slep
comments.text:
## /lets:team Test Session 2026-03-03

### Setup
4 tasks in parallel (quick fixes), team 'quick-fixes-v2'.
Dependencies: #2 blocked by #1 (both touch end.md), #4 blocked by all (touches all files).

### What worked
- **Plan mode + approval flow** - agents submit plans, lead reviews and approves. Clean cycle.
- **Dependencies** - agent-summary spawned only after agent-fast completed #1. agent-revparse waited for all 3.
- **Inter-teammate awareness** - agent-summary read fresh end.md after agent-fast modified it. agent-revparse read all files fresh after all teammates finished.
- **Graceful shutdown** - agents shut down cleanly after task completion.
- **Task claiming** - agents claimed tasks via TaskUpdate (owner + in_progress).

### What needs improvement
- **No isolation worktrees** - agents worked directly in the same worktree (no isolation: worktree). Changes were live, no merge step. Works for non-conflicting files but risky for overlapping edits.
- **agent-revparse plan timing** - it submitted plan summary as a regular message, not via ExitPlanMode. Had to nudge it to resubmit formally when blockers cleared.
- **Idle spam** - agents send multiple idle notifications after finishing. Minor noise.
- **Shutdown race** - first shutdown_request to agent-revparse didn't register (agent was busy?). Needed second request.
- **beads tasks not auto-updated** - agents don't run bd update on beads tasks. Lead had to mark beads tasks in_progress manually before team started.

### Observations
- Plan mode adds ~30-40 sec per agent (read + plan + submit + approve). Worth it for medium tasks, overkill for trivial fixes.
- For truly parallel work with file conflicts, isolation: worktree + merge is needed.
- Agent count sweet spot: 3-4 parallel. More = more lead coordination overhead.
- Non-isolated mode works great when tasks touch different files.

title: Audit agent dispatch: decide where to use teams vs subagents
description:
## Task
Review all agent dispatch points across commands and decide where Agent Teams add value vs where Task() subagents are the right tool.

## Current dispatch map

| Command | Mechanism | Agents | Count | Interactive? |
|---------|-----------|--------|-------|-------------|
| /lets:review (code) | Task() parallel | up to 11 from catalog | 3-11 | No |
| /lets:review (plan) | Task() parallel | architect + pragmatist | 2 hardcoded | No |
| /lets:opinion | Task() parallel | 3-5 from catalog | 3-5 | No |
| /lets:brainstorm Step 4 | Task() parallel | explorer | 1 or 3 | No |
| /lets:brainstorm Step 6 | Task() parallel | architect | N per approach | No |
| /lets:brainstorm Step 7 | Task() parallel | pragmatist + domain | 2-5 | No |
| /lets:ask | Task() single | any 1 from catalog | 1 | No |
| /lets:team | Agent() parallel + worktree | implementer | N per task | Yes |
| /lets:pr | delegates to /lets:review | - | - | No |
| /lets:check | inline, no agents | - | 0 | No |

## Decision criteria
- Fire-and-forget analysis (no follow-up needed) -> Task() subagents
- Interactive (lead wants follow-ups, discussion, steering) -> Agent Teams
- Write-capable (code changes) -> Agent Teams + worktree
- Single question/answer -> Task() single
- Speed critical (check) -> inline, no agents

## Questions to answer for each dispatch point
1. Does the user ever want to ask follow-up questions to a specific expert?
2. Would experts benefit from seeing each other's findings?
3. Is the overhead of TeamCreate/shutdown justified?
4. Could this become /lets:discuss invocation instead of inline Task() calls?

## Strong candidates for Teams

### /lets:brainstorm Step 7 (Expert Evaluation) -> /lets:discuss
Related: lets-d742e (Create /lets:discuss)
Users often want to dig deeper into specific expert findings. Currently fire-and-forget means you lose the experts after they report. With teams:
- Ask security-expert to elaborate on a risk
- Ask pragmatist to respond to architect's complexity concern
- Steer evaluation toward specific aspect user cares about
- Reject evaluation and ask expert to look at something specific

### /lets:review plan mode -> /lets:discuss or team-based review
Currently hardcoded to architect + pragmatist (2 agents, fire-and-forget). Real experience shows plan review benefits from interactivity:
- User records plan review, gets findings, wants to ask 'what about X?'
- Reviewer flags concern but user wants clarification before deciding
- Plan touches security/DB but only architect+pragmatist review it (not adaptive)
With teams: adaptive expert selection + follow-up questions + deeper discussion on flagged concerns.

### /lets:review code review -> possibly hybrid
11 agents fire-and-forget works well for initial scan. But after getting results, user often wants to:
- Ask specific expert to look at a particular file more closely
- Challenge a finding ('is this really a security issue?')
- Get expert's opinion on a proposed fix
Could be: Task() for initial scan, then /lets:discuss for follow-up on specific findings.

## Keep as subagents (no change)
- /lets:opinion -> designed as quick parallel poll. If user wants interactivity, they should use /lets:discuss instead
- /lets:brainstorm Step 4 (exploration) -> fire-and-forget, results feed into next step. No interactivity needed.
- /lets:brainstorm Step 6 (architecture) -> fire-and-forget, results presented to user for selection
- /lets:ask -> single agent, no team needed. Quick ping.
- /lets:check -> inline by design, speed is the point

## Not candidates
- /lets:pr -> delegates to review, no own agents
- /lets:execute -> sequential by necessity, no agents

## Anomalies found
- git-historian missing from /lets:opinion and /lets:brainstorm Step 7 catalogs
- explorer only used in /lets:brainstorm, not available via /lets:ask
- Plan review (review.md) hardcoded to 2 agents, not adaptive to plan content

## Deliverable
Decision document: for each dispatch point, keep Task() or migrate to /lets:discuss (when built). Update commands accordingly.

## Related tasks
- lets-elhe6: --worktree flag for /lets:team
- lets-d742e: /lets:discuss command
close_reason: Merged into lets-csc1o (Polish /lets:team v2 - as audit first step)

title: Investigate mode: plan bypass in Agent Teams
description:
## Bug
mode: 'plan' parameter on Agent() spawn does not reliably enforce plan approval.

## Evidence
- Smoke test 1: 2 teammates with mode: plan -> both sent plan_approval_request (WORKED)
- Smoke test 2: 1 teammate with mode: plan -> no plan_approval_request, directly edited + committed (FAILED)
- Same model (haiku), same agent type (lets:implementer), same spawn pattern

## Investigation needed
1. Does mode: plan work with custom agent types (lets:implementer)?
2. Is it model-dependent? Test with sonnet
3. Is it intermittent / race condition?
4. What does mode: plan actually enforce? (read Claude Code docs)

## Fallback options if unreliable
- PreToolUse hook blocking Edit/Write until plan approved
- Prompt-level enforcement (stronger wording in teammate prompt)
- acceptEdits mode instead of plan (less restrictive but reliable)

## Impact
Without reliable plan enforcement, /lets:team cannot guarantee lead review before code changes.
close_reason: Merged into lets-csc1o (Polish /lets:team v2 - mode:plan resolved, no code change needed)

comments.author: Dima Slep
comments.text:
## Debug results 2026-03-02

### Confirmed: mode: plan is prompt-level only (NOT tool enforcement)

Tested with minimal prompt (no mention of ExitPlanMode):
- haiku + mode: plan -> bypassed, edited directly
- sonnet + mode: plan -> bypassed, edited directly

### Why smoke test 1 worked
The full teammate prompt template in team.md has explicit section:
'PLAN FIRST - You are in plan mode. Read relevant code, understand existing patterns,
then propose your implementation plan. The lead will review and approve before you can make changes.'

This prompted the model to call ExitPlanMode. mode: plan alone does nothing.

### Resolution
- mode: plan is harmless, keep it as hint
- Real enforcement = teammate prompt template (already exists)
- No code change needed - team.md already has the right prompt
- Downgrade from P1 bug to P3 documentation issue
- model: haiku unreliable for plan mode even with prompt - use sonnet (already default in implementer.md)

comments.author: Dima Slep
comments.text:
## Architecture Design (v2 - deferred)

Full CLI with dispatcher + lib/ structure. Designed and reviewed by architect, pragmatist, security, devops experts.

### Structure
scripts/lets/
  install.sh, bin/lets (dispatcher), lib/statusline.sh, lib/fetch-usage.sh,
  lib/init.sh, lib/update.sh, lib/version.sh, lib/common.sh, VERSION

Installed to ~/.lets/{bin,lib,cache,VERSION}

### Key decisions
- POSIX sh dispatcher with exec routing
- Global cache ~/.lets/cache/ (usage per-account)
- jq for settings.json manipulation
- Config template embedded in init.sh heredoc
- Self-update via VERSION comparison + re-download

### Expert findings to address when implementing v2
- DevOps: MANIFEST file instead of duplicated file list, staging dir for atomic update
- Security: validate LETS_HOME not symlink, show diff before update, pin to tagged releases
- Pragmatist: only build when 5+ subcommands justify a dispatcher

### Decision
Deferred in favor of pragmatist approach (v1): single merged statusline.sh + install.sh.
Revisit when lets needs more subcommands (init, discuss, research, etc).

Subagent-driven approach gives fresh context per task, enables parallelizing independent tasks. Requires creating a lets:implementer agent (write-capable, unlike existing read-only agents).

Design note: see beads comment on 4ef about subagent-driven-development reference skill.

title: Add failure handling for parallel agent dispatches in review and opinion
description: Systemic issue found during brainstorm review: review.md and opinion.md have no failure handling when parallel agents fail/timeout. Unlike brainstorm (where data flows are chained), these commands can lose one agent perspective silently. Add guidance for what to do when an agent fails: note the gap, continue with remaining agents, mention missing perspective in output. Acceptance criteria: review.md and opinion.md both handle agent failures gracefully, following the project rule 'stop, explain, options, wait'.

title: Improve context window management rules and token optimization
description:
Current Context Window Management section in rules-context.md is minimal (3 lines). Need to expand with practical guidelines:

1. Audit rules-context.md for token waste (duplications, verbose examples, sections that could be shorter)
2. Better thresholds and actions for context management
3. Consider which sections could move to on-demand loading vs always-injected

Related: pragmatist review found that rules-context.md already has duplication and verbose examples costing unnecessary tokens every session.

title: Review /context reminder placement across all commands
description:
The 'Check context window: /context' reminder appears at wrong moments in workflow commands. Example: in /lets:done it shows before the confirm question (Step 5) when user can't act on it yet.

Need to audit all commands that show this reminder and decide:
1. Where exactly it should appear (end of flow? only in /lets:end?)
2. Should it be in every command or just session lifecycle commands (start/end)?
3. Maybe it belongs only in rules-context.md as a general rule, not hardcoded in individual commands

Audit: done.md, end.md, start.md, and any other commands that mention /context.
close_reason: Batch fixes commit af1c515
